claims.text: The proposed alloy is an equiatomic CoCrFeNi base modified with 5 at.% W and 3 at.% Al.
High-energy ball milling produces a random FCC solid solution in the stated Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-W-Al powder mixture.
Aging at 700°C after solution treatment forms nanoscale coherent B2-ordered NiAl precipitates in the FCC matrix.
W segregates to grain boundaries in the processed alloy.
Oxidation produces a protective Cr2O3/Al2O3 dual-layer film.
W addition increases the stacking-fault energy of the alloy.
W stabilizes the B2 phase at lower temperatures.
Al promotes formation of a protective alumina scale.
The 700°C aging treatment drives B2-NiAl precipitation.
Coherent B2-NiAl precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase hardness.
The B2-NiAl precipitate network impedes oxygen diffusion and thereby improves oxidation resistance.
W-enriched grain boundaries prevent intergranular corrosion.
The processed alloy will have a Vickers hardness greater than 500 HV.
The processed alloy will have a density greater than 8.5 g/cm³.
The alloy will exhibit an oxidation mass gain below 0.5 mg/cm² after 100 hours in air at 800°C.
The alloy will exhibit a corrosion current density below 1 µA/cm² in 3.5 wt.% NaCl at 25°C.
The identically SPS-processed unmodified CoCrFeNi baseline typically has a hardness of approximately 250 HV.
The unmodified CoCrFeNi baseline forms a comparatively less protective Cr2O3 scale that is prone to high-temperature spallation.
Keeping the aging temperature below 750°C prevents formation of brittle sigma phases.
W contents above 8 at.% promote TCP phases that degrade toughness and corrosion resistance.

contradictions.description: The composition is described as containing 5 at.% W and 3 at.% Al, but the stated nominal formula Co20Cr20Fe20Ni20W5Al3 totals only 88 at.%, so it is not a valid atomic-percent composition as written. If W and Al are fixed at 5 and 3 at.%, respectively, the four equiatomic base elements would each be 23 at.%.

The headline hypothesis invokes a W-enriched passive oxide scale, whereas the detailed mediator and mechanism place W primarily at grain boundaries and identify the oxide as a Cr2O3/Al2O3 film. The proposed location and oxidation role of W are therefore internally inconsistent or insufficiently reconciled.
